claims: Issue #606 reports s(146) <= 12.583782190152, the exact rational side of search/packer/candidates/tt2_n146.cert rounded up at 12 places, 1.38e-8 below Robert Barnett's 12.583782203951 (#505, a refinement of Ryan Xu's #432); it prints the certificate side 12.583782190151860342292508597077 with the SHA-256 of tt2_n146.cert and of tt2_n146_regularized.cert, the same packing regularized for display at the same side.

The side is the 80-digit KKT point S* = 12.58378219015186034216... scaled by 1 + 1e-20 about the origin corner; the issue calls the packing a different local minimum from #505's, strict modulo 59 exact flat motions against #505's 61, with 13 rattlers, 69 corner-corner contacts and no corner-corner MILP descent, matching #505 to about 1e-7 except a cluster of 10 squares tilted near 42 degrees; these are numerical evidence at 80 digits, as the issue says, not interval proofs.

The issue says the packing came from a time-travel test of the author's chain search started from the public packings of 10 October: two random large perturbations of Ryan Xu's #432 packing and a re-polish reached 12.5837821905, and one exact descent step (MILP direction, then re-polish) reached the certified minimum; it asks that Ryan Xu's #432 packing be credited as the start and Robert Barnett's #505 as the record it improves.

No closed form (elimination leaves irreducible factors of degree 15 to 32), no interval proof of local optimality and no optimality claim; the source's verify_cert.py and verify_cert2.py accept both files, and this repository's sqpack.verify was not run by the author.
